crates.name: trasic-scene
crates.owns: Validated conceptual scene descriptions, semantic IDs, domain value types, provenance references, and schema.

crates.name: trasic-sdl
crates.owns: Sources, tokens, spans, Logos adapter, syntax nodes, expression parsing, and neutral syntax/evaluation request types.

crates.name: trasic-eval
crates.owns: Evaluation driver, scopes, expansion frames, language coercions, semantic lowering, and scene finalization.

crates.name: trasic-geometry
crates.owns: Geometry preparation, intersections, inside queries, CSG event policy, and acceleration.

crates.name: trasic-texture
crates.owns: Texture preparation and point/context sampling with explicit resource bindings.

crates.name: trasic-render
crates.owns: Camera rays, sampling, transport, reconstruction, tile scheduling, and film commits.

crates.name: trasic-cli
crates.owns: Commands, configuration, filesystem adapters, budgets, output, and diagnostic presentation.

crates.name: trasic-conformance
crates.owns: Development-only reference-process adapters, fixture manifests, canonical comparison, and evidence bundles.

external_rules: Combobulate adapters live with the geometry/render consumers; Polars is not a dependency of scene or SDL.
Statelet observes explicit transitions owned by Trasic; it does not dispatch or validate them.
Neither upstream library takes a production dependency on Trasic.
A runtime-to-proc-macro edge must never combine with a reverse production edge.
The reference C++ process and conformance harness are not production-renderer dependencies.

requirements.statement: Reproduce the selected modern hgpovray scene semantics under an explicit profile.
Validate language, geometry, texture, and rendering boundaries independently.
Preserve source and expansion provenance in comprehensible diagnostics.
Use and evolve Combobulate for legible, bounded domain composition.
Use and evolve Statelet without transferring machine ownership.
Make resource, numerical, compatibility, and partial-completion policies explicit.
Tie delivery and compatibility claims to reproducible, non-vacuous evidence.
